source_refs.note: Topic 2.7.1 Working with Modules (PDF 55-56, printed 52-53). The book's function name say_As-Salaam-Alaikum is invalid Python; the conversion fractions print as '|'. Long question 7 is answered. Recorded.

blocks.text: A module is a file of Python code, such as functions, variables and classes, that can be reused in other parts of a program. To create one, write the code in a file and save it with the .py extension.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)

blocks.text: Running main.py imports greetings, calls its function and prints 'As-Salaam-Alaikum, everyone!'. The book names the function say_As-Salaam-Alaikum, which is not a valid Python name because names cannot contain hyphens; the lesson uses say_salaam.

blocks.prompt: Create a module temperature_converter.py with celsius_to_fahrenheit(c) and fahrenheit_to_celsius(f), and use it from main.py to convert 25 C and 77 F (long question 7).
blocks.explanation: In temperature_converter.py: def celsius_to_fahrenheit(c): return 9 / 5 * c + 32 and def fahrenheit_to_celsius(f): return 5 / 9 * (f - 32). In main.py: import temperature_converter as tc; print(tc.celsius_to_fahrenheit(25)) gives 77.0 and print(tc.fahrenheit_to_celsius(77)) gives 25.0. (The book prints the fractions 9/5 and 5/9 as '|'.)

items: A module is a .py file; import it and call its functions; keep main() as the starting point.
